claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances and your children.

Let me start with the first question:

**How many children are you looking to claim Child Benefit for?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, I'm looking to claim for one child - my son Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're looking to claim Child Benefit for your son Alex.

To help assess your eligibility, I need to gather some details about Alex and your circumstances.

**What is Alex's date of birth?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's 9 years old - born in 2016.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. So Alex was born in 2016 and is currently 9 years old.

**Does Alex live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't live with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I see. That's an important detail. 

**Can you tell me who Alex currently lives with?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He lives with his mum.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. So Alex lives with his mum, not with you.

**Are you Alex's biological or adoptive parent?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm his biological parent.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. Before I can give you a final answer, I need to understand the living arrangement a bit better.

**Do you have any financial responsibility for Alex, such as paying maintenance or child support to his mum?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do help out financially. I contribute towards his upkeep - things like clothes, school expenses, that sort of thing.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that detail. I need to gather a bit more information to give you an accurate answer.

**Is Alex in full-time education, or does he attend school full-time?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's in school full-time - he's only 9, so he's in primary school.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. That's helpful to know. I have one more important question:

**Did Alex's mum (or anyone else looking after Alex) claim Child Benefit for him before you started contributing financially, or is she currently claiming it?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, his mum is already claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that information. I now have enough details to assess your eligibility. Let me review the official Child Benefit rules to give you an accurate answer.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the official Child Benefit rules I've just reviewed, I can now provide you with my assessment:

**Unfortunately, you are not eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:

According to the Child Benefit eligibility rules, **only one person can get Child Benefit for a child**. Since Alex's mum is already claiming Child Benefit for him, you cannot also claim for him.

While the rules do allow someone to continue receiving Child Benefit for a child who lives with someone else (if they're making financial contributions to that child's upkeep), this only applies when **nobody else is claiming** for that child. 

In your situation, Alex's mum is already actively claiming Child Benefit for him. This means you cannot make a claim, as only one person can receive Child Benefit for the same child at any given time.

If you and Alex's mum wanted to change who receives the Child Benefit, you would both need to contact the Child Benefit Office to discuss transferring the claim to you, but this would require her agreement and for her to stop claiming.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about this?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Oh, I see. That's disappointing, but I understand - only one person can claim at a time. No, I think that's clear, thank you for explaining it to me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
You're welcome! I'm glad I could clarify the situation for you. It's understandable that it's disappointing, but you now have a clear picture of how the rules work.

If circumstances change in the future – for example, if Alex's living arrangements alter or his mum's circumstances change – do feel free to contact the Child Benefit Office to discuss your options. They can provide additional guidance on your specific situation.

Thank you for using this service, and I wish you all the best!
